The assumption that there is no air resistance is a standard simplification in introductory physics to make projectile motion calculations tractable using constant acceleration equations. However, in real-world scenarios, air resistance (drag) significantly affects the trajectory, causing the projectile to travel a shorter distance and reach a lower maximum height than predicted by the idealized model. Additionally, assuming gravity is perfectly uniform is an approximation that holds well for short distances but becomes less accurate over very large scales where gravitational variation matters. The claim that initial velocity remains constant until the projectile leaves the launching device is also a simplification; in reality, the projectile accelerates within the barrel or launching mechanism.

The animal with distinctive black and white stripes is the zebra.
